summary: The remaining v46 lit-candle split screen difference is caused by the missing light.c:obj_split_light_source() call during mkobj.c:splitobj(). When a lit candle stack is split for a drop, C attaches a second light-source node to the child and sets child.lamplit; the JavaScript caller currently records note_unported and leaves the child unlit, omitting the "(lit)" part of its drop name. Port the whole light.c function in js/light.js and call it from js/obj.js:splitobj() after timer splitting.

source.branch: When src has an LS_OBJECT node in gl.light_base, C copies each matching light-source node to dest and prepends it to gl.light_base. For candles it recalculates the source and destination ranges with candle_light_range() and sets vision_full_recalc; for every matching source it changes the copied id to dest and marks dest.lamplit=1. The admitted recipe lights a five-candle stack, then drops one candle so mkobj.c:splitobj() reaches this call with a live candle light source.
callers: C direct caller: mkobj.c:splitobj():501 checks obj_sheds_light(obj) and calls obj_split_light_source(obj, otmp) after obj_split_timers; C discards the helper result.

JavaScript owner: js/obj.js:splitobj() performs the same predicate and ordered call, but the active game path currently replaces the helper with note_unported("light.c obj_split_light_source"). The command path is apply.c:use_candle -> use_lamp -> begin_burn, then do.c:doddrop -> drop -> mkobj.c:splitobj; JavaScript paths are js/apply.js:use_candle/use_lamp -> begin_burn and command dispatch -> js/do.js:doddrop/drop -> js/obj.js:splitobj.
dependencies: light.c:candle_light_range() is already implemented in js/light.js and is used for both candle radii.
light.c:obj_sheds_light() is already implemented in js/light.js and remains the exact caller predicate.
No other direct C call site exists for obj_split_light_source(); mkobj.c:splitobj() is its sole active caller.

selectionReason: Selected the next unreserved mismatch from saved combined queue SHA-256 e381a612fbd22667de87ac4a6627c90a0f4164c63559cd4be9d84ee756b8a3b2 after the troll-meal delivery. Current v46 reservations assign the swamp session to B, prayer/furniture to C, and prior shopkeeper/troll sessions to A2. This lit-candle case is independent; its queue owner is unset, and source tracing identifies light.c:obj_split_light_source().
evidence: The saved v46 entry identifies one unmatched screen at segment 0 step 24, key n, with no RNG or cursor mismatch. The C recording step says "You drop a partly used candle (lit)."; direct current-head replay run-nUUpYO reproduces the mismatch at boundary 25: C has a blank at row 0 column 29 while JavaScript has a period. Their PRNG values, screen counts, and cursor positions match.

nethack-c/upstream/src/light.c:779-803 copies a matching LS_OBJECT node, updates candle radii through candle_light_range(), requests vision recalculation, prepends the cloned node, and marks dest.lamplit=1. Its sole C caller is nethack-c/upstream/src/mkobj.c:501-502, reached after timer splitting in splitobj().

js/obj.js:954-958 has the same obj_sheds_light() position and order, but only invokes an optional splitObjectLight hook; the game path falls through to note_unported("light.c obj_split_light_source"). Consequently the child made by splitobj() remains lamplit=false, and objnam.js formats the drop message without the C "(lit)" suffix.

Source scope is the whole light.c:obj_split_light_source() plus its existing JavaScript caller wiring in js/obj.js. The complete helper can reuse the existing candle_light_range(), obj_sheds_light(), and gl.light_base representation in js/light.js; no extra C family is required.
